name: MO-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+27 partisan lean makes this among the most Republican seats in the country
Smith holds a massive financial edge: about $5.5 million on hand versus roughly $12,500 for Reichard
No public polls or expert ratings treat the race as competitive; markets price Smith near 98 percent
model.rationale: The R+27 district lean, Smith's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 98 percent Republican all point to a comfortable incumbent win, and no polls or raters suggest otherwise. The only real uncertainty is turnout in a low-attention race, which is unlikely to come close to closing a twenty-plus-point gap.
model.watch: A major scandal, sudden outside spending against Smith, or a sharply altered national environment could narrow the margin, though nothing currently signals any of these.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Missouri's 8th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, and Jason Smith has held it easily since 2013. He enters the general election with about $5.5 million on hand after raising more than $6 million, while Democrat Chris Reichard has raised roughly $25,000. No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters list it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Smith about a 98 percent chance of winning, consistent with the district's partisan lean and the lopsided fundraising gap. A Libertarian candidate, Rebecca Sharpe Lombard, is also on the ballot, but third-party presence has not historically changed outcomes here. The forecast expects Smith to win by roughly 22 points, with uncertainty driven mainly by turnout in a low-attention contest rather than any sign of a genuine race.
